Thanks for the context — I reviewed MediPort’s redline and SIG. Summary and recommended stance below (high level):

1) Retention (PHI):
- HIPAA-aligned customers often request longer retention windows. From an operational and risk perspective, we prefer limiting retention to what is necessary for the service (default 3 years) but will accept a contract carveout if the customer can demonstrate regulatory need for 7 years for PHI.
- Proposed text: "For PHI subject to applicable law requiring longer retention, Parties will document the lawful basis and retention period in an addendum; Redwood will implement retention controls consistent with such addendum only to the extent technically feasible and scoped to the customer’s account."

2) Subprocessors:
- We will provide a current subprocessor list and a 30-day notice for new subprocessors. We push back on an unlimited opt-out right because it would block operational improvements.
- Proposed compromise: 30-day notice + right to terminate for material changes affecting data residency or PHI processing. This narrows the opt-out to high-impact changes.

3) SCCs / International Transfers:
- We can sign the EU SCCs (modular controller-to-processor flow) or an equivalent Addendum. Need Procurement to confirm whether MediPort wants the standard SCC language or an alternate.

4) Audit / Evidence:
- We will deliver SOC 2 Type II report and can provide a read-only audit window under NDA for formal audits. For vendor questionnaires, we can provide a completed SIG spreadsheet and answers.

5) Signature & escalation:
- Recommend two-step acceptance: AE-level confirmation to proceed + DocuSign for legal signature. If the final redline includes non-standard commercial credits or SLA deviations that exceed threshold X (to be defined by Finance), escalate to VP Sales/GC.

Action items I’ll take: prepare a redline proposal with the language above and a short negotiation memo. Marissa / Karthik, please flag any commercial concessions you can authorize (retention, credits, SLA).

Attachment: Proposed_Redline_MediPort_DPA.docx (internal legal redline)

Lauren Bishop
